This file is already the Fortran-side interop shim for all of Mods (its own header comment: "Remove this FORTRAN interface subroutines once the transition to C++ is complete"). C++ calls INTO it: software/mcfm/src/BLHA/CXX_Interface.cxx:34-36 declares extern "C" void modules_fi_init_() / modules_fi_finalize_() and calls them at lines 171/175. That is a genuine Fortran interop boundary, which the triage note says to keep.

Blocking facts:
1. All 58 callees are Fortran MODULE procedures with no C binding. grep over software/mcfm/src/Mods/*.f90 finds 58 "<mod>_mod_init()" definitions and zero with bind(C); same for the *_finalize routines. Their linker names are gfortran-mangled (__nwz_mod_MOD_nwz_mod_init), not name_. The Spec's fallback ("if the callee is still Fortran, declare the plain Fortran symbol in extern \"C\"") covers plain external subroutines, not module procedures, so calling them from C++ would require writing ABI-mangled names that appear nowhere in the source. No precedent exists: grep -rn "_MOD_" across all .cpp/.cxx/.hpp under src/ returns only unrelated include-guard hits in Mods/ckm_mod.hpp.
2. The work these routines do has no C++ counterpart. Each binds a Fortran module pointer to C++-owned storage, e.g. Mods/nwz_mod.f90 does "call c_f_pointer(get_nwz(), nwz)" against nwz_mod::nwz defined in Mods/nwz_mod.cpp. C++ cannot perform that binding.
3. Every module still has a live Fortran half (all <mod>.f90 AND <mod>.cpp are listed in Mods/CMakeLists.txt), so the binding is still required by every Fortran caller in the tree. Replacing this file with C++ would leave all 58 Fortran module pointers null while the build still passes and the tests print nothing -- exactly the silent segfault the Spec forbids.

Unblocking condition: this file becomes actionable only once the Fortran halves of the Mods modules are retired, at which point modules_fi_init_/modules_fi_finalize_ should be DELETED rather than translated. WHAT THE UNIT IS. /home/akash/Desktop/Akash/Projects/JSS-Paper-Example/software/mcfm/src/Mods/types_mod.f is `module types` and contains nothing but four compile-time kind selectors: `integer, parameter :: sp/dp/ex/qp = selected_real_kind(6/15/18/33)`. No variables, no procedures.

WHY THE ASSIGNED PATTERN CANNOT APPLY. The triage note prescribes .hpp + .cpp + _fi.f90 mirroring variables via c_f_pointer, following ewcouple_mod/couple_mod. That pattern is categorically inapplicable here, for three compounding reasons:
1. Nothing to mirror. Every symbol is a `parameter`. The convention baked into every generated Mods header states: "Within the extern \"C\" interface expose variables that do not have `const` attribute." Parameters get no extern "C", so the .cpp would be empty and c_f_pointer would have no address to bind.
2. A Fortran language constraint, not a style choice. `dp` is a KIND selector: `real(dp)` requires a compile-time constant expression. A `pointer` obtained via c_f_pointer is a runtime entity and cannot legally appear as a kind. gfortran would reject all 298 use sites. The only _fi.f90 that would compile is one re-declaring `integer, parameter :: dp = selected_real_kind(15)` verbatim — a rename producing zero C++, which would also collide as a duplicate `module types` or, if the original were moved, record TRANSLATED against no translated code.
3. Moving it to deprecated/ breaks the build wholesale. 166 live files (298 `use types` statements) still depend on it: W2jet 66, BDK 40, Mods 21, Z2jet 16, ThreeJets 16, loop 3, plus W/W1jet/Procdep/gghgg_dep. Critically, 21 are Mods modules still Fortran-only in the build and listed in CMakeLists — constants_mod.f90 (`real(dp),parameter:: pi=...`), mxpart_mod.f90, nf_mod.f90, zeta_mod.f90, heldefs_mod.f90, blabels_mod.f90 and others. build_roadmap.py also excludes */deprecated/*, so the module would silently vanish from the index.

THE REPO'S SETTLED CONVENTION IS TO NOT TRANSLATE THIS FILE. The conversion instructions embedded in the already-translated Mods headers say verbatim: "Ignore the `use types` statement since it will not be available in C++." Accordingly every settled header carries `#include <types.hpp>` COMMENTED OUT (e.g. Mods/ewcouple_mod.hpp, b0_mod.hpp, lc_mod.hpp, Cabibbo_mod.hpp), and no types.hpp exists anywhere under src/ (the only `#include <types.hpp>` hits are in scratch dirs W1jet/gpt-4o-conversions/ and ThreeJets/working/, both EXCLUDE_PATTERNS). This is consistent with the Spec's own rewrite table, which maps `real(dp)` directly to `double`: module `types` is absorbed into that mapping, so its correct C++ counterpart is nothing. It can only retire after the last `use types` disappears — the end of the transformation, not now.

result.notes:
NOT TRANSLATABLE BY CONSTRUCTION — needs a human/Plan decision to exclude it from the ready set permanently. No files changed; no build, no test, no CMakeLists touched.

Why it must stay Fortran:
1. It already IS the Fortran-side `_fi` interop shim the Spec's own Output shape prescribes ("a `_fi.f90` that mirrors variables via c_f_pointer"). Its two entry points already carry `bind(C, name="modules_fi_init_")` / `bind(C, name="modules_fi_finalize_")`, and C++ is the caller, not the callee: /home/akash/Desktop/Akash/Projects/JSS-Paper-Example/software/mcfm/src/BLHA/CXX_Interface.cxx declares them at lines 35-36 and calls them at 171 (ctor) and 175 (dtor). Translating it to C++ would delete the Fortran side of a boundary C++ depends on.
2. Verified mechanically, not just asserted: all 60 callees are plain Fortran module procedures with ZERO `bind(C)` — I checked every one (`subroutine <m>_init() bind(` matched 0/60; the only `bind(C)` in those modules is on the imported `get_*` getter interfaces, i.e. the C++->Fortran data direction). Calling them from C++ would require inventing gfortran-mangled names like `__pp_mod_MOD_pp_mod_init`, which appear nowhere in the source — forbidden by the Spec's "Never invent a called symbol."
3. Removing it would leave all 73 remaining Fortran module shims in src/Mods with null `c_f_pointer` targets — Spec trap #9 (silent segfault, no `passed` marker) rather than a clean FAILED.

Its `deps=0 blind=0 fanin=0` roadmap row (`Mods/Modules_Interface.f90	Mods	0	0	0`) is an indexer artifact: `use <mod>, only: <proc>` + `call <proc>()` is not counted as a dependency edge, so it wrongly surfaces as a ready leaf. Recommend the Plan/roadmap exclude it (like Need/Inc infrastructure) rather than re-offering it each round.

Why no C++ artifact is defensible:
- The module's entire body is four kind parameters: sp/dp/ex/qp = selected_real_kind(6/15/18/33). A kind is an intrinsic-evaluated integer with no source-level value, so `const int dp = 8;` would invent a compiler-specific constant and `using dp = double;` would invent a type where the source has an integer. Both violate the Spec's "Never invent a symbol, call, or interface the source does not already have."
- The Spec's rewrite table already absorbs real(dp)/complex(dp) into double/std::complex<double>, so `dp` is consumed at translation time and never reaches C++.
- A .cpp/_fi c_f_pointer mirror (Spec's module Output shape) is illegal Fortran: a kind must be a compile-time constant, and there are no non-const variables to expose in extern "C".
- An empty include-guard-only types.hpp would resurrect a header every generated Mods header deliberately comments out ("Ignore the `use types` statement since it will not be available in C++") and would add no symbol.
